idea: a CLI todo app with local storage

plan.summary: A command-line todo app that stores tasks locally and supports add, list, complete, and delete operations.

phases.name: Setup & Core Structure
steps: Create project directory and initialize git repo
Set up Python virtual environment
Create main entry point script (cli_todo.py or similar)
Create storage module to handle JSON file read/write operations
Define todo data model (task, description, status, timestamp)

phases.name: Core Commands
steps: Implement 'add' command to create new todos with description
Implement 'list' command to display all todos with status indicators
Implement 'complete' command to mark todos as done by ID
Implement 'delete' command to remove todos by ID
Add help/usage documentation for each command

phases.name: Storage & Persistence
steps: Create JSON storage file in user's home directory or config folder
Implement save-to-file logic after each command
Implement load-from-file logic on app startup
Handle file creation if storage file doesn't exist
Add error handling for corrupted JSON

phases.name: Polish & Testing
steps: Add input validation for todo descriptions and IDs
Improve terminal output formatting (colors or tables if desired)
Test all commands manually (add, list, complete, delete)
Test edge cases (empty list, invalid IDs, special characters)
Add basic error messages for common issues

phases.name: Distribution
steps: Create setup.py or pyproject.toml for package metadata
Add shebang and make script executable on Unix
Document usage in README with examples
Test installation and execution from outside project directory

idea: a CLI todo app with local storage

plan.summary: A command-line todo application that lets users add, list, complete, and delete tasks, persisting data locally in a JSON file so tasks survive between sessions.
stack: argparse (stdlib) or click for CLI parsing

phases.name: Project Setup
steps: Initialize a new git repository and create a virtual environment (python -m venv venv).
Create project structure: todo_cli/ (package), todo_cli/__init__.py, todo_cli/cli.py, todo_cli/storage.py, todo_cli/models.py, tests/, README.md, requirements.txt, setup.py or pyproject.toml.
Add click and rich to requirements.txt and install via pip install -r requirements.txt.
Set up pyproject.toml with entry_points so the CLI can be invoked as 'todo' command after installation (pip install -e .).

phases.name: Data Model & Storage Layer
steps: Define a Task dataclass in models.py with fields: id (int), description (str), done (bool), created_at (ISO timestamp), completed_at (optional ISO timestamp), priority (optional str: low/medium/high).
Implement storage.py with functions: load_tasks() -> list[Task], save_tasks(tasks: list[Task]) -> None, get_storage_path() that resolves to ~/.todo_cli/tasks.json (create directory if missing).
Implement JSON serialization/deserialization helpers converting Task dataclasses to/from dicts.
Add auto-incrementing ID logic based on max existing ID + 1 when adding new tasks.
Handle corrupted/missing JSON file gracefully by initializing an empty task list and writing a fresh file.

phases.name: CLI Commands
steps: Implement 'todo add <description> [--priority low|medium|high]' command that creates a new Task and appends it to storage.

Implement 'todo list [--all|--done|--pending] [--sort priority|created]' command that prints tasks in a formatted table (id, status checkbox, priority, description, created date) using rich.table if available, else plain text.
Implement 'todo done <id>' command that marks the specified task's done=True and sets completed_at timestamp.
Implement 'todo delete <id>' command that removes the task with the given id, with confirmation prompt unless --force flag is passed.
Implement 'todo edit <id> [--description TEXT] [--priority LEVEL]' command to update an existing task's fields.
Implement 'todo clear-completed' command to bulk-remove all tasks marked done.
Add a top-level --version flag and helpful --help text for each subcommand via click decorators.
Ensure all commands print clear error messages for invalid IDs or malformed input, exiting with non-zero status code on failure.

phases.name: Polish & UX
steps: Add color coding for priority levels and strikethrough/dim styling for completed tasks when rich is available.
Add confirmation messages after each mutating command (e.g., 'Added task #4: Buy milk').
Support relative date display for created_at (e.g., 'today', '2 days ago') using a small helper function.
Add a config option (env var TODO_CLI_HOME or --data-dir flag) to override default storage location for testing/multiple lists.

phases.name: Testing
steps: Write unit tests in tests/test_storage.py covering load/save round-trip, missing file initialization, and corrupted file recovery.

Write unit tests in tests/test_cli.py using click.testing.CliRunner to test add/list/done/delete/edit commands end-to-end against a temporary storage directory (use pytest tmp_path fixture and monkeypatch TODO_CLI_HOME).
Add tests for edge cases: deleting non-existent id, marking already-done task, listing empty list.
Run pytest and ensure all tests pass with >90% coverage on storage.py and cli.py.

phases.name: Packaging & Documentation
steps: Finalize pyproject.toml with project metadata, dependencies, and console_scripts entry point 'todo = todo_cli.cli:main'.
Write README.md documenting installation (pip install -e .), usage examples for each command, and storage file location.
Add a CHANGELOG.md with initial version entry.
Tag initial release v0.1.0 in git.

manual_checklist: Install Python 3.11+ on the target machine if not already present.
Decide whether to publish the package to PyPI (optional) and reserve the package name if so.
Verify write permissions for the user's home directory (~/.todo_cli/) on target OS (Windows path differences may need testing).

idea: a CLI todo app with local storage

plan.summary: A simple command-line interface application for managing basic to-do lists stored in a local JSON file.

phases.name: Phase 1: Project Setup and Data Persistence
steps: Initialize a Node.js project: run `npm init -y`.
Create a dedicated JSON file (`todo_data.json`) in the project root to store the todo list data. This file should start with an empty array: `[]`.

Write a utility function (`loadTasks`) that reads the `todo_data.json` file synchronously or asynchronously, handling potential file read errors (e.g., file not found) by returning an empty array instead of crashing.
Write a utility function (`saveTasks`) that takes the current array of todo items and writes it back to `todo_data.json`, ensuring proper JSON formatting.

phases.name: Phase 2: Implementing Task Addition
steps: Create the command handler logic for adding a task (e.g., command: `todo add "Task description"`).
The application must prompt the user or accept the task content as a command-line argument.

Develop the data structure for a single task item: it must include at least `id` (a unique integer identifier, incrementing on every add), `description` (string), and `completed` (boolean, default `false`).
Implement the logic to create the new task object and prepend/append it to the list of tasks.
Integrate task adding: After creating the new task in memory, use the `saveTasks` function to immediately write the updated list back to `todo_data.json`.

phases.name: Phase 3: Listing and Viewing Tasks
steps: Create the main command handler for listing all tasks (e.g., command: `todo list`).
This function must load the list of tasks using `loadTasks()`.
Iterate through the loaded array of tasks.

For each task, print a formatted output to the console that clearly displays: 1) The task ID, 2) The current status (e.g., **[DONE]** or **[TODO]**), and 3) The description. Formatting should differentiate between completed and incomplete tasks (e.g., using strikethrough or separate color codes if supported).
Implement basic filtering: Ensure the listing function can handle displaying all tasks without additional arguments.

phases.name: Phase 4: Completing and Managing Tasks
steps: Create the command handler for marking a task as complete (e.g., command: `todo complete [task_id]`).
Validate the input: Check if a valid `task_id` was provided and if that ID exists in the current task list.
If the ID is valid, locate the corresponding task object in the array, and update its `completed` status property to `true` (or `false` if implementing uncompleting).
After modifying the task object in memory, use the `saveTasks` function to write the modified list back to `todo_data.json`.
If the ID is invalid, display a user-friendly error message indicating the ID was not found.

manual_checklist: Ensure Node.js is installed on the local machine. The developer should test the CLI functionality directly from the terminal.
